_meta.note: Each trap has real PYQ examples. Use these in blueprint generation to inject specific trap strategies per skeleton.

traps.name: low_cloud_warming_vs_cooling_effect
traps.description: States low clouds cause a COOLING effect — they actually cause WARMING by absorbing infrared radiation from Earth.
traps.mechanism: Students know high clouds (cirrus) cool by reflecting sunlight. They assume all clouds cool. Low clouds trap outgoing radiation = warming.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: 'Low clouds have high absorption of infrared radiation from Earth's surface and thus cause a warming effect' — TRUE. Students who assumed clouds always cool marked this wrong.
traps.how_to_generate: Use cloud types (high/low/middle) and assign wrong radiation effects (reflection vs absorption, solar vs terrestrial radiation).

traps.name: congo_basin_carbon_sink_lung_confusion
traps.description: Tests whether students know Congo Basin (not Amazon) is the world's largest carbon sink.
traps.mechanism: Amazon is called 'lungs of the Earth' in popular media. Congo Basin is actually the largest net carbon sink per scientific measurements.
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: DRC / Congo Basin — 'known as lungs of Africa, largest carbon sink in world, absorbing more carbon than Amazon' — correct per UPSC's answer.
traps.how_to_generate: Ask about superlatives for carbon sinks, biodiversity hotspots, or forest cover using either Amazon or Congo. Students will default to Amazon for most superlatives.

traps.name: cobalt_mining_byproduct_wrong
traps.description: States cobalt is primarily mined as a standalone mineral — it's actually a BYPRODUCT of copper and nickel mining.
traps.mechanism: Students know cobalt is used in batteries and DRC is the main producer, but don't know the extraction method (byproduct, not primary mine).
traps.real_pyq_example: 2024: 'Cobalt is primarily mined as a byproduct of nickel and copper mining' — TRUE. Students who thought cobalt has dedicated mines marked this wrong.
traps.how_to_generate: Use any strategic/critical mineral (cobalt, lithium, rare earths). Ask about primary vs byproduct extraction. Many critical minerals are byproducts.

traps.name: ramsar_wetland_criteria_wrong
traps.description: States a specific criterion for Ramsar designation that is slightly wrong — especially the 20,000 waterbird threshold.
traps.mechanism: Students know Ramsar is about wetlands but not the exact criteria numbers and conditions.
traps.real_pyq_example: Recurring PYQ type: 'A wetland qualifies for Ramsar listing if it regularly supports 20,000 waterfowl' — this IS one of the criteria but students mark it wrong because they think it's arbitrary.
traps.how_to_generate: State the actual numerical criteria with a slight modification (10,000 instead of 20,000, 1% instead of actual threshold). Or swap Ramsar criteria with IUCN criteria.

traps.name: treaty_body_wrong_secretariat
traps.description: Assigns the secretariat of an environmental convention to the wrong city/organisation.
traps.mechanism: CITES (Geneva), CBD (Montreal), UNFCCC (Bonn), Ramsar (Gland, Switzerland) — students mix up host cities.
traps.real_pyq_example: Recurring: 'CITES secretariat is located in' — options include Geneva, Nairobi, Montreal, Bonn. Students confuse with UNEP (Nairobi) or IPCC (Geneva).
traps.how_to_generate: Match environmental conventions to their secretariat cities. Include two that are in the same city or same country to increase confusion.

traps.name: ozone_vs_greenhouse_gas_confusion
traps.description: Claims ozone IS a greenhouse gas — it IS, but students think it's not because its main role is UV protection.
traps.mechanism: Students learn about ozone for UV protection and never connect it to greenhouse warming. But ozone IS a greenhouse gas in the troposphere.
traps.real_pyq_example: PYQ multi-statement type: 'Tropospheric ozone is a greenhouse gas' — TRUE. 'Stratospheric ozone is a greenhouse gas' — also technically true but less impactful. Students mark both wrong.
traps.how_to_generate: Use any gas that has dual or unexpected roles (ozone, water vapor, methane vs CO2 comparison by GWP). Ask about its classification in a way that requires knowing the secondary role.
